observations: Death route carries 12 boxes (Nitro field + checkpoint): the box gem requires a no-death run to the fork.
The perfect run is a loop: the death route skips half the normal course, which must be ridden backwards.
Checkpoints are placed for the loop: mid-skipped-half (C3), junction (C4), and one on the death route.
Speed pads aim the player through crate rows and straight at the next hazard.
Both masks precede trap-dense zones; the second is guarded by Nitro (method matters).
Crates next to hives make the player stop where a chasing bee arrives.
The burrow verb is taught by crates that break from below.
The bonus is a vertical tool puzzle with the only 1UP crate.
One green switch after the junction clears three Nitro groups.
Second cross-level link: the warp plant to Road to Ruin's hidden section.

geometryObservations: Seeds turn static islands into timing steps. Islands (≈ 2-3 u) sit in pits that plants target; the safe moment is right after the burst (POINT 3; D2 s6, s26, s30). The gaps are trivial (≈ 1-1.5 u), so the timing is the whole test.

Speed pads are aimed. Each pad breaks a crate row and then points the player straight at the next hazard (stone head, fork, fence) — the pad's direction is a designed line (S1-e, S2, S3-a). Walking back, the pads push the wrong way (D2 s38).
Fences are stacked one coupling at a time: a double fence (POINT 6) → trapped between fences with seeds still landing (POINT 7) → fence + hive (POINT 12) → a pit hidden behind the current (POINT 13).
The hidden pit behind a fence (POINT 13) is a deliberate visibility trap with a named answer: the slide-jump, a long jump through the gate window.
Mines escalate from avoidance to knock-back: fields to jump or skirt (S1) → dense mines where bees catch up (S3 POINT 11) → mines on the lip of a pit, where a blast knocks you in (S5 POINT 19).
Bees are pursuers that punish stopping: hives sit next to crates, mine fields and fences, so every stop to break a crate or wait for a fence lets a bee arrive; F2 says kill one first.
The burrow is taught on a wide, walled, crate-filled stretch (crates break from below, POINT 16) before it is used against bees (POINT 17) and plants (POINT 15: from below = 1 fruit, a slam = 9).

Path width is a dial: ≈ 4-5 u main path; a ≈ 2-3 u bridge with chasms on both sides for the mask-in-front-of-Nitro beat (the careful verb); a narrow road at the end where bees come from behind (POINT 21).
The death route compresses the main course: ≈ 2 u pillar islands in deep pits with seeds and bees, a Nitro field at the entrance, and its own checkpoint halfway.

The perfect run walks the course backwards (F2 p098R: S4 → S3b → fork → junction), so the geometry has to work both ways: pits are symmetric, speed pads become obstacles, bees arrive from the camera side.
Every enemy has its own verb: plants (body slam or underground spin), bees (spin on arrival), stone heads (avoid; read the face), hammer workers (spin above ground), mines (jump).
Rest pads are explicit: the bonus plate + C2 and the C4 junction are wide, enemy-free pads, and the checkpoint after the hidden pit (C3) is the 'very welcome' save for the backtrack.
geometryTransfer: Seed-timed island. A 2.3 × 2.3 m island in a `pit` with 1.2-1.7 m gaps to the banks, targeted by a `sentry` whose projectile bursts on the island; on foot the jump is trivial and the burst window is the test. Repeat it later with the opposite instruction (jump just before the burst).

Aimed speed pad. A `speedpad` that lifts the board above the 12.5 m/s smash threshold, pointed at a 3-crate row along the line, with a `charger` or `pendulum` 10-15 m beyond — the pad commits the line. Keep plain crates ≥ 5 m apart if the row should be smashed in one pass.

Gate with a hidden pit. A timed barrier (`firetiki` jet or `phasepad`) across the path with a ≈ 3 m `pit` just behind it, readable only when the barrier is off; the answer is a long jump (5.6 m on foot) through the off window.
Mines on a pit lip. A field of explosive hazards on the take-off of a 2.5-3 m `pit`, so a triggered blast pushes the player in; make field + pit one jump (6.6 m board ollie at cruise).
Pursuer that punishes stopping. A homing `hopper` released from a hive-like spawner next to every crate cluster; the player has to kill it before collecting.

Reverse-rideable branch. If the perfect route requires backtracking, keep the bypassed half symmetric (no one-way drops) and place `speedpad`s to the side of the line, so that ridden backwards they are avoidable rather than walls.
